articles.body: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Dr. Laura Keesman, Assistant Professor of Sociology at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Dr. Keesman examines the complex relationship between peaceful protest, radical activism, social inequality and state authority. She challenges the tendency to interpret disruptive demonstrations exclusively through the lens of extremism. Even when protesters engage in confrontational or unlawful actions, she argues, their motivations may remain rooted in genuine political and socioeconomic grievances.

articles.body: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Steven Erlanger, Chief Diplomatic Correspondent in Europe for The New York Times, based in Berlin. Europe's political centre is confronting a crisis that extends far beyond electoral volatility. From France and Germany to Italy and Spain, mounting economic frustration, generational inequality and declining confidence in established political leadership are reshaping the continent's democratic landscape. "The promises of more economic growth haven't come true," explains Erlanger, describing a continent marked by "a kind of general disgust" and "a sense of drift."
articles.headline: 'Popular dissatisfaction' across Europe: 'Promises of more economic growth haven't come true'

articles.body: With less than two weeks until Election Day, most statewide debates have come and gone. Democrats tried to paint their Republican opponents into corners over loyalty to President Donald Trump, and Republicans tried to stake out nuanced positions on the Iran war and data centers. Here’s what we learned from the more than two dozen statewide candidate debates that occurred — and from those that didn’t. Republicans walk a fine line with an unpopular Trump In debate after debate, Democrats tried to tie their opponents to the unpopular president. Republicans weren’t always willing to let them. Several candidates — especially in blue states — were willing to break with the president. In New Hampshire, GOP former Sen. John Sununu said he’s “never met President Trump” and emphasized he’s “never hesitated to stand up to my party or the president when they're wrong,” specifically criticizing Trump’s policies on trade, Iran and Ukraine. In Minnesota, Republican Senate nominee Michelle Tafoya said she disagreed with Trump’s tariff policy and immigration enforcement, and when asked if she would appear onstage with Trump, she demurred. “I am talking to Minnesotans. Theirs is the only endorsement that I care about,” she said. In Maine, GOP Sen. Susan Collins emphasized that she has voted against the president more than 100 times this year, and criticized his approach on Iran. Bobby Charles, the GOP nominee for governor and a former official in President George W. Bush’s State Department during the Iraq and Afghanistan wars, said he disagreed with Trump’s “extended engagement” in Iran because “I know what it means to get stuck in a place.” Some Republicans became frustrated by their opponents' efforts to tie them to the president. “He wants to make this about Donald Trump,” said former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) “The bingo game ought to be, how many times can he put the word ‘Trump’ in any answer that he has given in the last, whatever, 30 minutes? It’s ridiculous.” But in some redder states, candidates were more willing to hug the president — recognizing support from his base will be critical to win . “We need the Trump voters to come out,” Sen. Roger Marshall (R-Kansas) said in a debate Wednesday. “Just like with my wife, I can disagree with her. Now, my wife is always right, and President Trump is not always right. But I do think that it's great that I have a relationship that I can pick up the phone and discuss with him the pros and cons of what he's contemplating.” It’s the economy, stupid Democrats hammered Republicans on affordability issues, blaming Trump’s tariff policy and Iran for spiking prices. In response, a few conceded some Trump policies were hurting them — while others tried to blame the last president. “That Bidenomics, that Green New Deal that my opponent voted for, that’s where all this inflation came from,” said Rep. Mike Collins (R-Ga.) in a Senate debate in early October. The other Collins, Susan, went the opposite way in blue-leaning Maine. “The bottom line is Troy and I both would have voted against the Canadian tariffs,” she said in an October 13 debate, after saying the Iran war was “not well thought out.” Rep. Ashley Hinson, the GOP nominee for Senate in Iowa, said she would pause the gasoline tax before acknowledging the effect of the war: "I trust in our U.S. military, the greatest fighting force in the world, to bring this to a close as quickly as possible, because I know people are being squeezed,” she said. Democrats largely sang the same tune on Trump’s policies. “These tariffs are crushing our state, and we'll repeal those tariffs,” said Sen. John Ossoff (D-Ga.). “The tariffs and the war in Iran has hurt Iowa more than any other state,” said state Rep. Josh Turek (D-Iowa). “If you appreciate having record diesel fuel prices … then I'd say vote for Roger Marshall,” said Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee running for Senate in Kansas. “If you want change, then I'd like to ask you to vote for me.” Everyone hates data centers Republicans and Democrats showed a remarkable similarity in their distaste for data centers even as their specific policy prescriptions diverged — a sign of the issue’s rapid ascent as a bipartisan bogeyman, even as Trump reiterates his support for them. Candidates from both parties called for local control. “Look, if you don't want a data center, I will stand up and defend it and make sure you don't get it,” said Rick Jackson, a Republican billionaire businessman running for Georgia governor. “Local communities know best,” said Hinson, the Iowa Republican. In Maine, both Senate candidates said guardrails should be installed to prevent the data centers from raising utility rates for local residents. In Iowa, both gubernatorial candidates — Democrat Rob Sand and Republican Zach Lahn — supported ending tax breaks for data center developers. In New Hampshire, both Senate candidates agreed with GOP Gov. Kelly Ayotte’s push for a statewide moratorium. “At the end of the day, it's up to our governor, our local leaders, to make decisions about any big infrastructure, transmission, power plants, new factories, and data centers should be treated just the same,” Sununu said. Gaffe gamechangers Debates can do candidates more harm than good, and some candidates had some cringey moments. In Alaska, Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola appeared to be reading from a notecard throughout a recent debate, giving her opponent, GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan, a chance to pounce. "We weren't supposed to get these questions beforehand, were we?" he asked the moderator. “You can’t cue-card your way through the Senate,” Sullivan later wrote on social media. Sullivan had his own moment a few weeks earlier when he peeked at Peltola’s answer during a lightning-round question, prompting laughter from the audience. “Happy to help, Dan,” Peltola wrote on social media . In Kansas, Marshall faced loud chats of “you don’t live here” during a debate at the state fair, while speaking about his residence in Kansas and his home in Florida . In Maine, Jackson said Collins should “shut up” after a protester interrupted the debate and Collins claimed the demonstrator was “obviously one of Troy's supporters." "Oh, shut up,” Jackson said. “I don't even know that kid." Collins has pounced on the moment to try to paint Jackson as a sexist hothead; Jackson later said he did not regret his outburst. In Iowa, Hinson responded to a question about ensuring the solvency of Social Security by slamming young people’s saving habits . “We also need to be talking about millennials saving money,” she said. “Millennials are the worst group of savers in the country right now and have the least amount of savings.” The debates that didn’t happen Fear of gaffes may have cost voters a chance to see their candidates square off, as the longstanding political tradition of campaign debates took another hit this cycle. In Senate battlegrounds across the country, nominees in both parties outright refused to join their opponents onstage or carefully ducked debates. In Texas, Attorney General Ken Paxton rebuffed invitation after invitation (including one from Fox News), even after Trump urged him to get onstage. In Ohio, the Senate candidates still haven’t reached an agreement to debate. In North Carolina, there is no debate scheduled between the major-party Senate candidates for the first time in nearly 30 years . There doesn’t seem to be a partisan division over who will and won’t debate. Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs and Ohio Democratic nominee Amy Acton refused to debate their opponents. So did GOP Gov. Greg Abbott of Texas and Sen. Tommy Tuberville of Alabama, who have rebuffed invitations to debate. “There’s so much difference between us, I mean, there’s no reason to get up there and argue about differences of opinion,” Tuberville, running for Alabama governor against Democratic former Sen. Doug Jones, told reporters in August. Andrew Howard, Jason Beeferman, Lisa Kashinsky, Aaron Pellish, Alec Hernandez, Erin Doherty and Jessica Piper contributed reporting.
articles.headline: The good, the bad and the unruly from over two dozen candidate debates

articles.body: A new company whose polls had influenced campaign decisions and helped shape the midterms narrative admitted that it was faking its polling data on Tuesday night, setting off a firestorm in the electionsphere. Wedgewood Polls, facing an imminent publication of an investigation from FiftyPlusOne showing it was fabricating its numbers, declared late Tuesday night that it had been an “experimental project” to show how an “entirely fabricated polling firm” could sway public opinion while painting themselves as the good guys. They’d left an impact and been included by multiple credible polling aggregators including The New York Times — and mentioned twice in POLITICO's Morning Score polling roundup. Speculation is flying about what, exactly, Wedgewood was trying to achieve, and there’s still little public information about the defunct company that had crowdfunded thousands of dollars for its fake data. Was it an effort to boost progressives Democrats in primaries? If so, were progressives or Republicans really behind it? Was it being used to game betting markets? Were top operatives using the bogus data to make spending decisions? Were aggregation accounts too quick to jump on posting the data? An email to the account listed on Wedgewood’s X account bounced back, and previous PDFs of polls that were tied to the account are no longer available online. Regardless of what Wedgewood said it was trying to achieve (they remain adamant the project “was never intended to sway an election or permanently mislead the public”) — pollsters, operatives and candidates alike said there were real world implications for posting fake data online. Mallory McMorrow, the unsuccessful Michigan Democratic Senate candidate who dropped out before her primary, said a fake Wedgewood poll that showed her crashing to single-digit support against Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens “dried up” donations, “devastated” volunteers and led to numerous calls to exit the race. “It killed us,” McMorrow wrote on X . “These were some of the absolute worst days on the campaign. Especially for my team. There are no words to explain the morale blow, and nothing I could do or say to my team to fix it.” Jennifer Holdsworth, a Democratic operative who ran a super PAC supporting McMorrow, said the Wedgewood poll “was used by several donors to pull back funding at a time we were being outspent by $80 million.” The account also posted a poll showing democratic socialist Francesca Hong leading in the Wisconsin gubernatorial primary, when there was scant public polling, something that contributed to the narrative she was ahead before the election (which she lost). They also posted a poll showing the Mississippi Senate race within reach, just before Democrats plowed money into the state. Scott Colom, the Democrat running for the seat, blasted the poll to his press list as proof there was “massive momentum” behind him. That led election watchers to argue that Wedgewood’s data was being used to make spending decisions in top outside groups, which elicited a response from Democrats’ main Senate super PAC. “Absolutely not. We don’t make spending or strategic decisions based on external polling,” Lauren French, a spokesperson for Senate Majority PAC, said on X . In its investigation, FiftyPlusOne said it had included Wedgewood in its aggregator because the firm was founded by people who had worked in the polling industry previously. There’s also been broad finger-pointing at the aggregator X accounts that post polls frequently — and sometimes without verifying their accuracy. “You posted our polls multiple times. If you suspected it was fake, why did you post our results?” Wedgewood’s account shot back after Polling USA wrote that “my suspicions about Wedgewood were correct.” The whole ordeal illuminates just how big a problem polling could be in 2028, where both parties will have presidential primaries and polling can shift the narrative on a dime. “What I’m concerned about is essentially information pollution, things that are either intended to skew prediction markets or just straight misinformation flying around,” Charlotte Swasey, a pollster for the Democratic group Searchlight, told POLITICO Magazine recently. “It would be really difficult, especially in a primary, to tell people that what they’re seeing about their preferred candidate isn’t real.” A version of this article first appeared in POLITICO Pro’s Morning Score. articles.body: INTIFADA FLARE UP: One of New York City’s most prestigious public high schools is facing backlash because a school-based socialist youth group co-signed a social media post declaring “Intifada Until Victory!” The Young Democratic Socialists of America chapter of Stuyvesant High School — along with YDSA chapters at Hunter College, the New School, City College and Lehman College — all signed onto an Oct. 8 Instagram post that accused the Democratic Socialists of America’s New York City chapter of silencing student activists who wanted to protest Mayor Zohran Mamdani over Israel. The groups accused the democratic socialist mayor of betraying the Palestinian cause and blasted his decision to keep NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch in her position, referring to her as a “Zionist billionaire.” The term intifada — which refers to violent uprisings against Jews in Israel — is viewed by many Jews as a call to violence against them. Moshe Spern, president of United Jewish Teachers — an advocacy group representing Jewish teachers and students across the city — is demanding the posts be removed immediately and that the YDSA group provide a public apology to the school community. “NYC public schools have seen hundreds of antisemitic and anti-Israel incidents since October 7, 2023,” he wrote in an email yesterday to Stuyvesant Principal Seung Yu and New York City Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels. “When a school-recognized club amplifies this rhetoric, it risks contributing to a hostile environment.” In the missive, Spern invoked Title VI — the federal law that bans discrimination based on race, shared ancestry and national origin — and demanded a review of the YDSA chapter’s charter, faculty adviser and recent activities for compliance. Spern also cited a chancellor’s regulation that states that student clubs operate under the principal’s supervision and must remain consistent with the school’s educational goals. Yu did not respond to requests for comment. Mamdani’s Department of Education also did not respond to Playbook. Spern told Playbook today that he has yet to receive a response from Yu. “To flat out ignore it is extremely irresponsible,” he said. The NYC-DSA defended the organization. “We support the right to organize,” NYC-DSA co-Chair Gustavo Gordillo said in a statement. “NYC-DSA did not organize or endorse this particular rally, but red scare tactics have never been effective tools for engaging with student movements.” The social media uproar is the latest flashpoint in ongoing tensions in the city over Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the war that followed. Mamdani, a longtime critic of Israel, was reluctant to condemn the term “globalize the intifada” on the campaign trail last year before finally saying he will not use the term . He also drew bipartisan backlash over his statement marking the third anniversary of the attack. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu labeled the mayor an antisemite , which Mamdani has denied. Mamdani, though, has also simultaneously faced backlash from pro-Palestinian activists who accused him of betraying the Palestinian cause by retaining Tisch, who’s Jewish and a self-described Zionist. Those critics have also criticized him for not doing enough to prevent local synagogues from holding events that promote land sales in Israel, some of them in the occupied West Bank. — Madina Touré From the Capitol Q’S LATEST: Gov. Kathy Hochul has a 55-41 lead over Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman, a Quinnipiac University poll released this afternoon found. That 14-point advantage is narrower than the 19-point lead Quinnipiac gave Hochul last month. But it’s more in line with the numbers from other pollsters: Marist found Hochul up by 11 two weeks ago, Emerson had Hochul up 12 in early October, and Siena measured her lead at 9 points last month. Despite Hochul’s lead, the Q Poll concluded Blakeman has an enthusiasm advantage. A total of 65% of his backers were “very enthusiastic” to support him, while only 33% of Hochul’s supporters said the same. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL LANDER DETAINED: Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander was detained today by Israeli security officials while harvesting olives in the West Bank. Lander, a self-described liberal Zionist and critic of Israel , said he went to the West Bank as part of the “Protect the Harvest” coalition to support Palestinians gathering crops. Rabbi Jill Jacobs, CEO of T’ruah, a progressive rabbinical organization, said she was also detained Wednesday, along with “approximately 80 American, Israeli, and international volunteers providing a protective presence for Palestinian farmers.” According to a press release from T’ruah, there were “approximately two hours of peaceful harvesting” until “Israeli forces declared the area a closed military zone” and detained them to transport them to a police station, despite the volunteers agreeing to leave. An Israeli military official told POLITICO that officers from the Israel Defense Forces and Border Police, along with local police, arrived at the scene because Palestinians did not submit a request to coordinate harvesting in that area, which is required ahead of time. The official added that the farm in question “requires only a small number of harvesters to collect its produce” and “the security establishment views the arrival of dozens of activists as an act intended solely to provoke, which undermines the harvesting process.” Lander was released “once the matter was brought to our attention” that he is a congressional candidate, the official said. Lander confirmed in a social media post that he was released with a “warning” because of his “public profile.” Read more from Madison Fernandez in POLITICO . articles.body: Georgia Republicans are counting on Rick Jackson to save them from a wipeout in November — if President Donald Trump doesn’t get in the way. The billionaire health care executive and political newcomer has spent nearly $200 million since he entered the Georgia governor’s race earlier this year. That’s boosted GOP hopes as many in the party have all but given up on the state’s marquee Senate race, where Rep. Mike Collins is struggling to close the gap against a formidably well-funded Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff. Republicans worry that their open contests for attorney general and lieutenant governor as well as control of the state general assembly could be in peril in a larger blue wave. But Jackson’s deep pockets are being tested against a difficult political environment for Republicans, weighed down by unpopular Trump actions, including the war in Iran. And some in the GOP worry that the president’s repeated visits to Georgia could only make the situation worse. “I don't know that Trump coming helps Republicans more so than it excites Democrats, especially in a wave election year, and so becomes and becomes a catch-22 for Republican candidates,” said Jason Shepherd, a former Cobb County chair who is supporting Jackson. One Georgia-based Republican strategist who is not involved in the gubernatorial race posited that Trump’s dual appearances in the state almost certainly did more harm than help. They, like others in this article, were granted anonymity to speak openly about the race to avoid reprisals. “Every piece of data that I've seen, it is not MAGA Republicans that are unmotivated to vote in this election,” the person said. “All the data that I've seen is that the undecideds in our marquee races, and specifically in the governor's race, have a very, very negative opinion of the president. So, I can't really rationalize a case for how it would be helpful.” Jackson, for his part, has carefully navigated his relationship with the president and has not publicly broken with him on policy like other battleground Republicans. But he has not mentioned the president in any of the nearly 150 ads he’s run in the general election, according to an analysis of data from tracking firm AdImpact. Shortly after the RNC announced that Trump would return to the state this weekend, Jackson’s team said in a statement that the candidate will be campaigning in a different part of Georgia. And during his only televised gubernatorial debate on Oct. 6 against Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, Jackson never name-dropped the president — despite his opponent invoking Trump’s name eight times. Instead, the Republican mentioned popular outgoing GOP Gov. Brian Kemp five times and focused on Bottoms’ tenure as mayor of Atlanta during the Covid-19 pandemic. “It’s been proven time and again that when the message is on Georgia, and the results under Brian Kemp and the conservative vision and road map that's been laid out here, that we win in Georgia. When the focus is on D.C. and personal politics, we lose,” said Cole Muzio, president of the conservative Frontline Policy Action group .  The Jackson campaign declined to comment for this story. “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement. Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, said in a statement that Republicans “are laser focused on winning, and our candidates will run the races necessary to best represent their districts and prevent Democrats from taking control." Jackson is one of several Republicans across the country who now must balance between keeping the president close enough to turn out Republican base voters, but not so closely as to alienate the center. Though many Georgia Republicans see Jackson as their de-facto ticket-topper, they don’t see his win as a guarantee against Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, in a finicky battleground state like Georgia. Jackson has outspent Bottoms nearly 5-to-1 in the final stretch of the race but still remains in a close race in public polling . And yet, without him, Republicans fear the bottom would have already fallen out on races up and down the ballot, given how poorly Collins is performing in polls against Ossoff. Republicans’ top Senate super PAC, Senate Leadership Fund, was dark in Georgia last week , a sign the race may be slipping out of reach. “If Rick Jackson weren't running, we would all be in a lot of trouble,” said Stephen Lawson, a Georgia-based Republican strategist and Jackson ally. “He’s our best hope at keeping the state red.” A second Georgia-based Republican strategist, who is working on other races in the state, underscored how Jackson’s money is keeping the party afloat. “There is no question in my mind that without the extra $150 million he spent in his general election, that the ticket would be lost,” this person said. “That is the only reason there's still a fight to be had.” But, this person cautioned, the race is still very much a toss-up, and Jackson’s victory will rely on a large share of Georgia voters choosing to split their ballots between Ossoff for Senate and Jackson for governor. Jackson’s allies are optimistic that a significant number of voters will do just that. A private statewide poll reviewed by POLITICO found that roughly 19% of Georgia voters say they are definitely or likely to cast a vote for at least one Democrat and one Republican — a potentially significant pool of crossover voters that could power two very different results in the marquee contests. Whether the sheer force of Jackson’s spending will prove successful enough to overcome Trump is a microcosm of the larger issue his party is experiencing across the country: National Republicans, flush with cash, hold an enormous financial advantage over Democrats. But money alone may not be enough to insulate candidates in battlegrounds or even in traditionally red territory. “I don't know that Republicans across the country should feel as bullish about the cash influx that we've gotten because it didn't work here,” said the first GOP operative. “In terms of actively moving races in our favor, it at least didn't work here.” In the last month, as Bottoms began to spend more heavily on the air amid Jackson's spending advantage, her campaign has noted that polling has started to move marginally in her favor — even if the race remains largely within the margin of error . Her high name ID, as well as cash spent after the primary to define her early, are helping. “Rick Jackson has spent $200 million in this campaign but all the money in the world can’t hide the fact that he would be a lackey for Donald Trump,” TaNisha Cameron, a spokesperson for Bottoms, said in a statement. “Despite being outspent, Keisha’s message is breaking through and she has the momentum in this race right when it matters." Jackson is making more of an effort to tie himself closely to Kemp, who won over moderates and independents in his 2022 reelection for governor and has an approval rating that sits 30 points higher than the president’s in Georgia, according to a recent poll by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . Kemp, for his part, has continued to be a presence on the trail for Jackson, including joining him on a statewide tour earlier this month and appearing in at least three TV ads for the campaign. But Jackson’s pathway to victory requires him to not only secure crossover voters that may support Ossoff in the Senate race or the type of voters who broke for Kemp, but also turn out the MAGA base who powered the president’s two presidential victories in the perennial battleground. The president is intent on still showing up for him. Shortly after Jackson dispatched Trump’s initially preferred candidate, Lt. Gov. Burt Jones, in June’s primary runoff, the president was quick to praise Jackson as standing “strong with ‘TRUMP.’” And in subsequent posts on Truth Social, Trump has called the health care executive a “good friend.” Trump, onstage Friday, called Jackson a “great businessman,” before adding: “I’ve been watching you, you are good, and he never did this before. He did it because he wants to straighten out things and he’s an amazing, an amazing story.” Aaron Pellish contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Rick Jackson is the GOP’s best hope in Georgia right now

articles.body: Republicans are banking on a massive cash edge to help save their majority in Congress. But they are losing much of that advantage in an important arena: broadcast TV ads. Republicans have spent $677 million on those ads across 10 key Senate battleground states, compared to $479 million by the Democrats. But the GOP’s money isn’t going nearly as far because they’re more dependent on outside groups that pay much higher rates than candidates. The disparity has helped Democrats stay in the fight for Senate control amid an onslaught of GOP outside spending. In Ohio’s Senate race, Republican groups make up 63% of the $218 million spent. But in spite of their nearly 2-to-1 spending advantage over Democrats, they make up just over half of ads that are on the airwaves, according to data from the tracking service AdImpact. In Texas, Republicans have outspent Democrats by a 3-to-1 margin but have aired just 58% of the ads. And in Michigan, the GOP accounts for 60% of the spending but just over half of the ads. A large part of this discrepancy comes down to the mechanics of broadcast advertising. Candidates, and now political parties thanks to a recent Supreme Court ruling, are entitled to significantly lower rates. That has allowed Democratic candidates — who have posted bonkers fundraising hauls — to offset much of the GOP advantage in super PACs. Republican Senate candidates, on the other hand, struggled overall with their fundraising. And some GOP outside groups bought their ad time later, when it was even more expensive. “There are limitations to the impact of ‘big money’ in politics,” said Sean Cooksey, a Republican and former chair of the Federal Election Commission. “It's a good demonstration of the economics of campaign fundraising. Hard dollars really just go so much further.” The disparity also shows “the Republican overreliance on outside groups,” said Ian Russell, a Democratic admaker. “You get an eye-popping dollar amount, but it doesn't actually translate into as many spots as you would think relative to a well-financed candidate,” Russell said. “[Republicans] were just hoping that they could spend their way out of everything that was going wrong for them. But the problem is, their issues run much deeper than a few ad buys can fix. Especially when you've got monster fundraising hauls from the Democratic side.” Republicans in House and Senate races have long been more dependent on outside groups and megadonors, and for multiple cycles have seen their cash advantage undercut by fundraising strength from individual Democratic candidates. But that trend is particularly pronounced this year given the combination of Republican super PAC money and their candidates’ struggles. In 2024, Republican outside groups spent only about 15% more than Democrats on TV ads across House and Senate general election contests, according to a POLITICO analysis of AdImpact data. This cycle, GOP outside groups have spent 7% more. In a few states, the discrepancy between dollars and airtime is less stark. Republicans account for 60% of the spending in Maine’s Senate race and an equal percentage of the ads, according to AdImpact. That’s in part because Sen. Susan Collins has outraised her Democratic opponent Troy Jackson over the whole cycle, although Jackson, who didn’t launch his campaign until July, raised far more in the third quarter. The numbers show the shifting dynamics of campaign strategy after the Supreme Court opened the floodgates to more spending from parties by granting them the lower advertising rate. Republicans have been faster to take advantage of the new rules: Major coordinated spending efforts from the NRSC and RNC have helped their side significantly this cycle. Republicans have far outspent Democrats on Senate party-coordinated Senate advertising, $90 million to $34.6 million across TV, radio and digital ads, according to data from AdImpact. “If I were the leader of either party, I would say you shouldn't give a dollar, you shouldn't give a single penny to these super PACs until you've maxed out to the party committee,” Cooksey said. Some Republicans say that strategic errors have contributed to erasing their cash edge. A number of GOP strategists have also privately griped that MAGA Inc. — one of the major outside groups backing their candidates — bought TV airtime too late, forcing them to pay even higher rates and further draining resources and increasing the price of reaching voters. Republicans fretted for months about whether Trump’s well-financed super PAC, MAGA Inc., would get involved . The group has since spent heavily but only launched its first general election ad buys in September. “There is no question MAGA Inc. should have bought ads earlier in the cycle,” said one national GOP operative who was granted anonymity to discuss party strategy, noting that rates across the country increase as Election Day nears. Other top GOP outside groups, like the Senate Leadership Fund and the Congressional Leadership Fund, made their early advertising reservations much earlier in the cycle than MAGA Inc. Trump allies waved away that criticism. A person familiar with the Trump operation’s midterm planning, granted anonymity to discuss strategy, said it’s "indisputable that the spending from the Trump political effort has kept us competitive in many Senate races.” MAGA Inc. declined to comment. Still, GOP outside groups are utilizing their cash advantage in some underappreciated ways. Republican super PACs have massively outspent their Democratic counterparts on mail — roughly $157 million to $35 million for the general election — according to a POLITICO analysis of independent expenditure filings submitted to the Federal Election Commission. That’s led by a whopping $44 million in spending on mail across 24 races from the Trump-aligned No Going Back PAC, along with $23.8 million across 20 races from Elon Musk’s America PAC. GOP-aligned super PACs have also spent more than Democratic ones on phone calls and text messages, the data shows.
articles.headline: Why Republicans’ massive cash advantage is evaporating on the airwaves

articles.body: BLAKEMAN’S (LACK OF) ENERGY PLAN: GOP gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman continued to hammer Gov. Kathy Hochul on rising energy costs today, promising to slash utility bills in half if he’s elected. The Republican, however, still has not offered up a policy proposal on how he’d go about doing that. “Kathy Hochul increased our utility rates 48 times in four years,” Blakeman said in upper Manhattan this morning. The Washington Heights press conference, which included former Gov. George Pataki, was heavy on rhetoric and relatively light on details. Afterward, Blakeman’s campaign would not spell out how exactly he plans to cut consumer utility costs and did not respond to a request for clarification about his claim that Hochul increased utility rates 48 times. (While the state’s Public Service Commission has approved increases in major utility rate cases during Hochul’s tenure, those hikes have been less than what the utilities requested .) “Donald Trump’s puppet, Bruce Blakeman … wants data centers raising your costs and said Trump was doing an ‘amazing job’ after he jacked up utility bills.” Hochul campaign spokesperson Sarafina Chitika said in a statement. “Two weeks from irrelevance, here’s what Blakeman won’t tell you: Governor Kathy Hochul delivered a billion dollars in energy relief, ten billion in tax relief, and made data centers pay for the energy they use.” The Nassau County executive described meeting the owner of a Bronx diner who told him the business would need to sell 1,000 burgers a month to pay its $16,000 utility bill. Blakeman said he would legalize fracking to help New Yorkers lower their energy bills fast. Aside from the fact that fracking doesn’t necessarily lead to lower utility bills and the reality that Blakeman would need buy-in from the state’s Democratic-dominated Legislature to do so, he insists that legalizing fracking could offer near-term relief from high energy costs. “I met with those same individuals and companies that are doing the extraction of natural gas in Pennsylvania. They told me they can be up and running in 60 days,” Blakeman said. “If Albany has the will to reduce people's utility bills … we can get it done in 60 days.” He pointed to Pennsylvania, arguing that the state has lower electric bills because it allows fracking. But he neglected to mention that Pennsylvania is not part of the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative — the carbon trading program of 11 eastern states, which Blakeman has pledged to withdraw from if he is elected. Pataki, the last Republican to serve as governor in the Empire State, spearheaded the creation of that initiative, which is commonly known as RGGI. “The concept is right, but the way it's being done in Albany is wrong,” Pataki said at the presser, accusing Albany of using RGGI as a “slush fund.” Even if New York did withdraw from RGGI, the benefit would amount to a 5% to 6% decrease on an average New York residential household bill, according to an estimate from National Grid — barely making a dent in the 50% Blakeman is promising to slash. Exactly how the state would cover the rest of his proposed cut remains unclear. Affordability, though, continues to be a key concern in Washington Heights, a largely Dominican neighborhood that Mayor Zohran Mamdani did well in during his ascent to victory last year. To drive their message home, the Republicans even attempted to make their pitch in Spanish. Pataki, much more practiced in this than Blakeman, talked about how much he loved the “barrio” when he was governor, describing Blakeman as a leader “muy fuerte.” “Gracias, hombre grande,” Blakeman exclaimed, before touting what he views as the GOP ticket’s immigrant bonafides — Saritha Komatireddy for attorney general and Joe Hernandez for comptroller. “Governor, your Spanish is better than my Spanish, and I grew up speaking it,” Hernandez praised Pataki. — Mona Zhang From the Capitol LABOR BOOSTS GOV: A coalition of public employee unions is joining the crowded roster of super PACs spending on the gubernatorial election. The New York Accountability Coalition has received $550,000 in recent weeks from the Civil Service Employees Association, Public Employees Federation, District Council 37, and CWA District One. It’ll soon spend that money to boost Hochul. The governor “is laser-focused on lowering costs for working families and investing in public services,” AFSCME’s Courtney Brunelle-Kim said. “Bruce Blakeman is just another pay-to-play politician. From now until Election Day, we’ll be working to ensure that voters in key districts know The Blakeman Record.” The super PAC spent $460,000 this spring helping Comptroller Tom DiNapoli as he faced two Democratic primary challengers. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL AD PULLED: A clean energy super PAC yanked a version of an ad airing in a competitive upstate House district after Republican candidate Anthony Constantino’s attorney complained the spot was defamatory. The group Invest In Tomorrow Coalition recently began airing the spot in the sprawling North Country House seat that accused Constantino — who runs a custom sticker business — of selling anti-police merchandise. “What do Anthony Constantino and violent anti-cop extremists have in common? They both think ‘kill the police’ is a good slogan,” the ad’s narrator says. Constantino’s attorney last week contacted a lawyer for the super PAC alleging the contents of the ad were false and defamatory. On Saturday, the group signaled it would suspend further distribution of the current ad. So far, the PAC has spent some $243,000 in the district in the last three days, according to AdImpact. “Anthony Constantino may lawyer up, but he can’t sticker over the truth: he’s gotten rich off selling vile merch, including hosting a listing for a ‘Kill the Police’ sticker and other anti-cop listings that are still active today ,” said Chris Coffey, a spokesperson for the group. “As a token of our gratitude and recognition of his desire to spread that message, ITC PAC is putting $250,000 more behind the original ad buy to make sure all of NY-21 knows the real Anthony Constantino.” The fight over the commercial comes as Constantino is trying to retain the seat being vacated by GOP Rep. Elise Stefanik. Polls have shown Democrat Blake Gendebien running competitively against the Republican, however, giving the race a surprising dose of uncertainty in the final two weeks. — Nick Reisman HOUSE HUNTING: Two New York battleground districts have again moved in Democrats’ favor, according to a nonpartisan election forecaster. Sabato’s Crystal Ball shifted Stefanik’s upstate seat from “likely Republican” to “leans Republican” today, as well as Democratic Rep. Laura Gillen’s Long Island district from “leans Democratic” to “likely Democratic.” The Stefanik seat covers a sprawling, deep-red area — though Democrats are feeling bullish in part because of the Trump administration’s tariffs impacting farmers there. Gillen faces a challenge from Hempstead Receiver of Taxes Jeanine Driscoll. Kamala Harris narrowly won that district in 2024, but Republicans are counting on tailwinds from Blakeman, the Nassau County executive, to boost down-ballot candidates. — Madison Fernandez IN OTHER NEWS — REAL ESTATE STRIKES BACK: A new organization called Built For New York hopes to promote the real estate industry’s interests in the wake of a pro-tenant political sweep in New York City. ( The New York Times ) — PAC ALERT: A coalition of Jewish Democrats from the Capital Region launched a state-level PAC dedicated to supporting liberal candidates who push back on anti-Jewish and anti-Israel forces. ( Jewish Insider ) — BOOZE BUCKS: Lily Fan, chair of the State Liquor Authority and a close Hochul ally, donated $40,000 to a pro-Hochul super PAC that’s run by people who lobby the liquor industry. ( New York Focus ) Missed this morning’s New York Playbook? We forgive you. Read it here .

articles.body: <p>La Guardia Civil ha registrado este jueves un edificio y una nave industrial utilizados por organizaciones de ayuda a migrantes en Ceuta en el marco de una investigación que indaga sobre un supuesto reparto de aerosoles de gas pimienta y armas blancas. Las pesquisas estudian si se incitó <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/al-menos-11-militares-han-resultado-heridos-en-enfrentamientos-con-inmigrantes-en-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/al-menos-11-militares-han-resultado-heridos-en-enfrentamientos-con-inmigrantes-en-ceuta.html">a migrantes a atacar a miembros de Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad</a>, según indican fuentes policiales. Hay ocho personas investigadas, según el auto judicial que ha autorizado las actuaciones, al que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS. Fuentes de No Name Kitchen y las Brigadas de Apoyo Mutuo, organizaciones que utilizan como sede los inmuebles registrados y a las que pertenecen las personas implicadas, rechazan las acusaciones y aseguran que su actividad se limita a la asistencia humanitaria y a la documentación de posibles vulneraciones de derechos. El operativo, durante el que se ha localizado a tres inmigrantes, sigue abierto. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/la-guardia-civil-investiga-a-miembros-de-dos-ong-de-ceuta-por-repartir-aerosoles-de-gas-pimienta-y-armas-blancas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2026-10-19/el-exconsejero-catalan-toni-comin-adelanta-su-regreso-de-belgica-e-ira-antes-a-madrid-para-poder-ser-eurodiputado.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/catalunya/2026-10-19/el-exconsejero-catalan-toni-comin-adelanta-su-regreso-de-belgica-e-ira-antes-a-madrid-para-poder-ser-eurodiputado.html">exconsejero catalán Toni Comín, fugado de la justicia española hace nueve años </a>como consecuencia de su papel en el proceso independentista, se ha presentado finalmente este jueves en Madrid para acudir a la Junta Electoral Central (JEC) y jurar la Constitución española para adquirir plenamente la condición de eurodiputado. A la salida, Comín ha querido restar trascendencia a ese gesto formal y lo ha catalogado como “una pataleta de mal perdedor” y “un derecho al pataleo” del Estado español: “Es una prueba más de que saben que hemos ganado. Confirma nuestra victoria”.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/toni-comin-tras-jurar-la-constitucion-en-el-congreso-este-derecho-al-pataleo-confirma-nuestra-victoria.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/X5E5UYGFQZA6XH4IV6336XZNKQ.jpg?auth=c4b33aee379089438ef1dbcd0437181ffaa169e6682b59c28aee5ec4e29ceb71" width="5085" height="2672" alt="Toni Comín, este jueves en el Congreso, tras recoger su acta de eurodiputado."></img>
articles.headline: Toni Comín, tras jurar la Constitución en el Congreso: “Este derecho al pataleo confirma nuestra victoria”

articles.body: <p>Reconocido como una de las <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-06-01/pablo-bustinduy-el-ministro-que-conquista-espacios.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-06-01/pablo-bustinduy-el-ministro-que-conquista-espacios.html">figuras más valoradas</a> en el espacio político de la izquierda, el ministro de Derechos Sociales, Pablo Bustinduy, asumirá la portavocía de la campaña de Frente Amplio para las elecciones del 29-N. La coalición, que integra a un total de 15 formaciones y encabeza Ada Colau, ha anunciado este jueves la nueva función de Bustinduy, quien durante más de un año ha sonado como uno de los preferidos para liderar la papeleta en la izquierda. Él ha rechazado esa posibilidad desde el principio, pero en las últimas semanas, especialmente, sí se había abierto a ocupar cualquier otra posición dentro de la candidatura. El ministro no está de momento en las listas, como tampoco formó parte de ellas en las generales de 2023. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-22/frente-amplio-aprovecha-el-tiron-de-bustinduy-y-lo-nombra-portavoz-de-campana.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Frente Amplio aprovecha el tirón de Bustinduy y lo nombra portavoz de campaña

articles.body: <p>Esperanza Aguirre, expresidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, entra en una enorme sala de vistas de la Audiencia Nacional sobre las 10.15 de este jueves. La antigua baronesa del PP, que aún mantiene una enorme influencia en las filas conservadoras, camina de seguido hacia los magistrados del tribunal que enjuician a Ignacio González, quien fuera su mano derecha durante años y su sucesor en el cargo. Mientras ella deja el bolso en el banquillo de los acusados (a solo cinco asientos de su exsubordinado) y silencia el móvil, él evita mirarla a la cara y centra la vista en un cuaderno de notas en blanco. Establecen así tantas distancias como las que marcará Aguirre en su breve declaración para desvincularse de las irregularidades atribuidas a González por el <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2021-05-26/el-juez-procesa-a-ignacio-gonzalez-por-amanar-la-adjudicacion-del-campo-de-golf-del-canal-de-isabel-ii.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2021-05-26/el-juez-procesa-a-ignacio-gonzalez-por-amanar-la-adjudicacion-del-campo-de-golf-del-canal-de-isabel-ii.html">presunto amaño de contratos del Canal de Isabel II</a> para la puesta en marcha de un campo de golf en las instalaciones de la empresa pública en el centro de la capital (un proyecto impulsado por la propia política popular y <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2021-07-05/golf-mordidas-y-tribunales-historia-de-la-lucha-vecinal-para-levantar-un-parque-de-madrid.html" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2021-07-05/golf-mordidas-y-tribunales-historia-de-la-lucha-vecinal-para-levantar-un-parque-de-madrid.html">desmantelado en 2021 tras una intensa lucha vecinal</a>). La expresidenta regional reivindica esa idea, pero asegura que no sabe nada del desarrollo de las obras.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/esperanza-aguirre-declara-este-jueves-como-testigo-en-el-juicio-contra-ignacio-gonzalez-por-el-caso-lezo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Aguirre reivindica la idea de las “canchas” de golf del Canal, pero se desvincula de las irregularidades en el juicio a su sucesor

articles.body: <p>España e Italia han acordado no prorrogar <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-07/el-gobierno-amenaza-con-represalias-a-italia-si-no-retira-los-controles-fronterizos-a-viajeros-procedentes-de-espana.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-07/el-gobierno-amenaza-con-represalias-a-italia-si-no-retira-los-controles-fronterizos-a-viajeros-procedentes-de-espana.html">los controles fronterizos que recuperaron el pasado mes de agosto</a> para los vuelos y las conexiones marítimas, coincidiendo con la crisis migratoria de Ceuta, según ha informado el Ministerio del Interior español. El Ejecutivo de Giorgia Meloni impuso esta medida el pasado 1 de agosto como respuesta a la entrada irregular a la ciudad autónoma de miles de migrantes procedentes de Marruecos a finales de julio, y el Gobierno español respondió el 9 de agosto <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-07/el-gobierno-amenaza-con-represalias-a-italia-si-no-retira-los-controles-fronterizos-a-viajeros-procedentes-de-espana.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-07/el-gobierno-amenaza-con-represalias-a-italia-si-no-retira-los-controles-fronterizos-a-viajeros-procedentes-de-espana.html">con medidas de control</a> en frontera similares que afectaban a los viajeros procedentes de Italia. Los grandes damnificados de este choque que ha durado más de dos meses han sido los numerosos viajeros que tenían a estos países como destino.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/espanol-e-italia-acuerdan-levantar-los-controles-fronterizos-a-vuelos-y-las-conexiones-maritimas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El próximo mes de diciembre, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-22/el-avance-de-vox-en-los-gobiernos-del-pp-de-la-nacionalidad-espanola-en-la-ley-de-vivienda-de-aragon-a-la-censura-en-castilla-y-leon.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-22/el-avance-de-vox-en-los-gobiernos-del-pp-de-la-nacionalidad-espanola-en-la-ley-de-vivienda-de-aragon-a-la-censura-en-castilla-y-leon.html">PP y Vox en Extremadura</a> van a aprobar los segundos presupuestos de la legislatura en la Asamblea regional. Unas cuentas que se encuentran en tramitación parlamentaria y donde se recogen, de nuevo, importantes recortes en organismos dependientes de la Consejería de Desregulación, en manos de Vox. En lo destinado al Consejo de la Juventud de Extremadura, los fondos van a reducirse casi a la mitad de la financiación autonómica para el próximo año. En concreto, la transferencia prevista pasa de 763.382 euros en 2026 a 392.635 euros para el próximo ejercicio, una reducción de 370.747 euros, equivalente al 48,6%. Entre los capítulos que más sufren, el destinado a gastos corrientes, el cual pasa de 352.703 euros en 2026 a tan solo 28.300 euros en 2027. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/los-presupuestos-extremenos-condenan-a-la-asfixia-al-consejo-de-la-juventud-y-a-la-cooperacion-internacional-al-desarrollo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Los presupuestos extremeños condenan a la asfixia al Consejo de la Juventud y a la cooperación internacional de la región

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/IRIJMNP7VFHQVFOKZHMIFXOF3A.jpg?auth=bbca6629bd4736dc11450b0a1c780b030f9f5401ff76e4a0bed8a22675515d37" width="1586" height="1060" alt="Un guardia civil custodia la casa cuartel de Santa Pola tras el atentado terrorista de ETA de 2002."></img><p>El juez de la Audiencia Nacional Antonio Piña ha propuesto sentar en el banquillo a cuatro exjefes de ETA por el atentado cometido, el 4 de agosto de 2002, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2022-03-29/la-audiencia-nacional-reabre-el-contra-la-cupula-de-eta-por-el-atentado-en-santa-pola-de-2002.html?outputType=amp" rel="">contra la casa cuartel de la Guardia Civil de Santa Pola (Alicante)</a>, que dejó dos muertos —uno de ellos, una niña de seis años— y más de medio centenar de heridos. Se trata de Juan Antonio Olarra Guridi, alias <i>Jokin</i>; Ainhoa Múgica Goñi, <i>Olga</i>; María Soledad Iparraguirre Guenechea, <i>Anboto</i>; y Félix Ignacio Esparza Luri, <i>Navarro</i>. Con ellos, ya son seis los exdirigentes de la organización terrorista procesados por este atentado, después de que en agosto de 2024 lo fueran Mikel Albisu Iriarte, <i>Antza </i>y Ramon Sagarzazu Gaztelumendi, <i>Ramontxo</i>. <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2022-07-28/el-juez-cita-como-investigados-a-seis-exjefes-de-eta-por-el-atentado-mortal-de-santa-pola.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2022-07-28/el-juez-cita-como-investigados-a-seis-exjefes-de-eta-por-el-atentado-mortal-de-santa-pola.html">Todos ellos están acusados de los delitos de asesinato, lesiones y daños terroristas</a>.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/el-juez-propone-juzgar-a-otros-cuatro-exjefes-de-eta-por-el-atentado-mortal-de-santa-pola-de-2002.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: El juez propone juzgar a otros cuatro exjefes de ETA por el atentado mortal de Santa Pola de 2002

articles.body: <p>Cuando se confirmó que Javier Milei volvía a España pero esta vez en plena precampaña electoral, el equipo de campaña del presidente del Gobierno, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/milei-participa-en-un-desayuno-informativo-en-madrid-durante-su-visita-a-espana.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/milei-participa-en-un-desayuno-informativo-en-madrid-durante-su-visita-a-espana.html">Pedro Sánchez,</a> no daba crédito. Parecía un regalo perfecto. Y lo fue. Hasta el alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida, del PP, admitió que el viaje era un caramelo para el presidente. “Pedro Sánchez será el primero que esté muy feliz por la propaganda que le ha dado Milei hoy, estoy seguro”, llegó a decir el regidor.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/milei-agita-la-campana-con-insultos-a-sanchez-y-abrazos-a-ayuso.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/PDSFY3KGTBFQTBL56LPM3DTUCE.jpg?auth=4ea5447448081b8c70e8503a2e21b8164642a01fe4b581916072ecd195b4ab17" width="4724" height="3151" alt="El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo (i) y el presidente de la Junta de Andalucía, Juanma Moreno Bonilla (d), este miércoles en Sevilla."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/YLSG74QT6RAONLJGMNLP66KXC4.jpg?auth=f1cc15409145f66eab338703da0f5d04d95e3e9dcda2df93aca4be7b1bddbf15" width="6000" height="4000" alt="El PSOE exhibe una lona en su sede de Ferraz durante la visita a España del presidente argentino, Javier Milei, este miércoles."></img>

articles.body: <p>No es la primera vez que sucede. Hace dos años, en junio de 2024, en la anterior visita de Javier Milei a España, Isabel Díaz Ayuso incomodó a Génova <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-06-19/ayuso-condecorara-a-milei-quien-vuelve-a-insultar-a-sanchez-antes-de-viajar-a-madrid-llamandolo-cobarde.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-06-19/ayuso-condecorara-a-milei-quien-vuelve-a-insultar-a-sanchez-antes-de-viajar-a-madrid-llamandolo-cobarde.html">al otorgar al presidente de Argentina la medalla internacional de la Comunidad de Madrid,</a> en un acto con toda la pompa del que fue ajeno el líder del PP. Ahora, en plena precampaña electoral, la presencia del histriónico mandatario latinoamericano vuelve a ser incómoda para el PP, salvo para la presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, que ha vuelto a reivindicarlo como un referente, al recibirlo calurosamente y exhibir complicidad con un abrazo mientras el líder de su partido lo ignoraba y ponía tierra de por medio con un acto en Sevilla centrado en las políticas de vivienda. Los populares son conscientes de que los insultos de Milei en Madrid a Pedro Sánchez, a quien llamó este miércoles “impresentable dictador”, pueden activar al electorado progresista, pero confían en que el impacto de la visita del presidente argentino se diluya porque aún faltan 40 días para la cita con las urnas. “Menos mal que ha venido ahora y no el 21 de noviembre, porque si llega a venir la última semana de campaña el escenario sería distinto”, admite un dirigente. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/el-pp-confia-en-que-el-impacto-de-la-visita-de-milei-se-diluya-el-29-n-si-llega-a-venir-la-ultima-semana-seria-distinto.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: El PP confía en que el impacto de la visita de Milei se diluya el 29-N: “Si llega a venir la última semana sería distinto”

articles.body: <p>Javier Milei ha convertido <a href="https://elpais.com/argentina/2025-07-27/los-insultos-y-las-agresiones-se-duplican-en-las-redes-sociales-de-argentina-alentados-por-milei.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/argentina/2025-07-27/los-insultos-y-las-agresiones-se-duplican-en-las-redes-sociales-de-argentina-alentados-por-milei.html">sus insultos</a> en una seña de identidad que levanta polvareda allí donde va. articles.body: Una setmana després d’activar els Bonus Consum, més de 70.000 barcelonins ja s’han registrat per obtenir-los. I d’entre tots ells, més de 14.000 ja els ha fet servir en alguna de les més de 1.900 botigues de barri que, de moment, s’han adherit a la iniciativa. La Pilar, de Sant Andreu, és una de les veïnes que s’ha beneficiat del descompte. Aquest dijous al matí ha pagat 50 € per un jersei que, sense el val de 10 € de l’Ajuntament, li hagués costat 60 € . Només ha hagut de registrar-se a la pàgina web del consistori per obtenir un codi QR que ha ensenyat a la botiguera a l’hora de pagar. També et pot interessar Com aconseguir i on gastar els Bonus Consum de 10 € abans que s’acabin Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura Incentiu per gastar més La iniciativa està ajudant els comerços de proximitat a fer caixa en un període de l’any (després de la tornada a l’escola) en què les famílies tenen la butxaca més escurada, explica l’Ana Sánchez, de la carnisseria J. Tena. “Els Bonus Consum animen la gent a comprar una mica més i, fins i tot, allò que a vegades no arriben a comprar”. “Funcionen bastant bé”, afegeix. De fet, hi ha clients que ho corroboren. L’Anton, que aquest dijous ha comprat a Carn + Carn del carrer Gran de Sant Andreu, confessa: “Pujaré una mica el consum per arribar almenys als 30 € “. És l’import mínim perquè es pugui aplicar el descompte. Són 10 € de regal que, segons l’Ajuntament, estan fent que de mitjana la gent es gasti 48,83 € en botigues de barri. Altres usuaris asseguren que “el descompte s’agraeix” en un context de gran escalada de preus. Més de mig milió d’euros en vendes En només una setmana s’han generat vendes valorades en gairebé 700.000 euros . Un cop gastat el primer val es pot optar a un total de dos descomptes més . Això sí, no són il·limitats i estan subjectes a un pressupost fix. Un cop s’esgoti, s’acabaran els descomptes, sense previsió de quan pot passar això encara. Després de les rebaixes de gener s’activarà una segona tongada de Bonus Consum amb les mateixes condicions. articles.body: Barcelona concentra 32 dels 100 barris que més diners dediquen a pagar el lloguer de tot Espanya, segons les darreres dades de l’Institut Nacional d’Estadística (INE). La despesa mitjana destinada a pagar l’habitatge a la ciutat assoleix el seu màxim a Pedralbes, amb 2.002 € mensuals . És la segona zona més cara de tot l’Estat. Completen el podi barceloní les Tres Torres , amb una despesa mitjana de 1.911 € i la zona oest de Sant Gervasi – Galvany , que es queda a certa distància, als 1.744 €. L’últim barri barceloní que consta a la llista és Provençals del Poblenou , amb un lloguer mitjà de 976 €. Són les darreres dades disponibles, corresponen al 2024 , el mateix any que va entrar en vigor el topall del lloguer , que regula els preus dels arrendaments a les zones tensionades com Barcelona. Es tenen en compte, només, les ciutats de més de 250.000 habitants i estan fraccionades per zones, que no necessàriament coincideixen amb els barris oficials. Més de 1.000 euros de diferència Entre el primer barri barceloní que consta a la llista, Pedralbes, i l’últim, Provençals del Poblenou , hi ha més de 1.000 euros de diferència . Concretament, 1.026 €. Els salts de preus són més acusats a les posicions més altes de la llista. Per exemple, entre l’oest de Sant Gervasi – Galvany (1.744 €) i Diagonal Mar i el Front Marítim del Poblenou (1.508), per exemple, hi ha 236 € de diferència. També et pot interessar Quant costaria un lloguer a Barcelona si no hi hagués un topall als preus? Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura En canvi, entre els barris que ocupen les darreres posicions, la diferència és molt més petita , d’entre 1 i 29 €. Si comparem l’est de la Sagrada Família (993 €) amb la zona que ocupa la posició següent, l’est de la Vila de Gràcia (992 €), el cost només varia d’1 €. I en aquesta mateixa línia, hi ha una diferència de preu semblant entre l’est de la Sagrada Família i el barri que té immediatament al damunt, la Salut (997 €). En aquest cas, són 4 €. Madrid, al costat de Barcelona A més de Barcelona, hi ha una altra ciutat que també predomina a la llista de l’INE: Madrid . La ciutat encapçala el rànquing: el barri de Recoletos és el més car d’Espanya amb un cost mitjà del lloguer de 2.037 € . Supera, per poc, els preus de Pedralbes. La capital espanyola ocupa 63 llocs a la llista. Entre les dues ciutats, acaparen 94 posicions . Només s’hi colen tres punts més del territori espanyol: un barri de Màlaga (posició 40), un altre de València (48) i quatre zones de Palma. articles.body: La 3a Jornada de la Plataforma per a l’Educació Mediàtica (PEM), celebrada avui dijous a la Biblioteca Sarrià – J. V. Foix de Barcelona, ha reunit experts, periodistes i representants d’entitats per reflexionar sobre l’ impacte de la desinformació en la democràcia i els reptes que planteja la irrupció de la intel·ligència artificial. La sessió, emmarcada en la Setmana Mundial de l’Alfabetització Mediàtica i Informacional de la Unesco, ha estat inaugurada per la presidenta de la PEM i vicepresidenta del Consell de l’Audiovisual de Catalunya (CAC), Laura Pinyol, i pel gerent de Biblioteques de Barcelona, Ferran Burguillos. Durant la jornada, Laura Pinyol i el director de Relacions Institucionals de la Xarxa Audiovisual Local (XAL), Xavier Casinos, han presentat el Manifest per unes polítiques públiques estratègiques d’alfabetització mediàtica i informacional (AMI) a Catalunya . El document reclama al govern de la Generalitat que situï l’alfabetització mediàtica al centre de l’agenda política i impulsi una estratègia estable per combatre la desinformació i reforçar el pensament crític de la ciutadania. També et pot interessar Barcelona crearà una unitat per combatre les notícies falses a les xarxes socials Marta Casals Torres Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura Educació mediàtica per a tots els públics La plataforma, integrada per una cinquantena d’entitats i institucions dels àmbits de l’educació i la comunicació, alerta de l’ augment de la desinformació i de la proliferació de continguts falsos a través de xarxes socials, plataformes digitals i serveis de missatgeria. Segons el manifest, aquesta situació posa en risc el dret de la ciutadania a rebre una informació veraç i contrastada. Una de les principals novetats de la proposta és que l’educació mediàtica no es limita als centres educatius , sinó que s’estén al conjunt de la població. El manifest defensa programes de formació per a infants, joves, persones adultes i gent gran , amb una atenció especial als col·lectius més vulnerables davant les bretxes digitals i informatives. També et pot interessar Polítics i xarxes: “Si no s’assessoren poden convertir-se en un mem i objecte de burla social” Andrea Cuerva Bonich 1 minut de lectura La desinformació afecta els processos electorals La conferència inaugural ha anat a càrrec de la investigadora del CIDOB Carme Colomina, que ha analitzat l’impacte dels algoritmes i de les plataformes digitals en l’accés a la informació. Colomina ha alertat que la desinformació i la polarització incideixen directament en la qualitat dels processos democràtics i electorals . La jornada s’ha completat amb dues taules rodones sobre la lluita contra la desinformació i la seva influència en el vot de la ciutadania, així com amb una exposició dedicada a l’alfabetització mediàtica i a l’ús responsable de les pantalles. Entre les entitats adherides al manifest hi ha betevé , que comparteix la demanda de la Plataforma per a l’Educació Mediàtica perquè l’alfabetització mediàtica i informacional esdevingui una prioritat de les polítiques públiques.
articles.headline: La Plataforma per a l’Educació Mediàtica reclama una estratègia pública contra la desinformació

articles.body: La seu de l’Institut d’Estudis Catalans acull aquesta setmana la primera reunió per revisar i redactar la nova Declaració Universal dels Drets Lingüístics. Es tracta d’un text que vetlla per les llengües minoritàries i per totes aquelles que no tenen garantida la seva conservació. Experts i intel·lectuals de tot el món són a Barcelona per debatre les millores i correccions que necessita el text definitiu. La cimera està organitzada pel Pen Català i el Centre Internacional Escarré per a les Minories Ètniques i les Nacions (Ciemen). També et pot interessar Irídia, Òmnium i l’ANC denuncien una “vulneració de drets lingüístics” en el judici de Roger Español Núria Granados 1 minut de lectura Les xarxes socials i la globalització, esculls per a les llengües minoritàries La trobada actualitza el text tenint en compte els reptes amb què moltes llengües conviuen actualment. Per exemple, un dels grans esculls són les xarxes socials, que homogeneïtzen les llengües majoritàries i agreugen la situació de la resta. Per això, els experts de la cimera parlen de persones amb més vulnerabilitat lingüística, que són aquelles que es comuniquen amb llengües que tenen risc de perdre força o, fins i tot, de desaparèixer. Jordi Garrell , director del Ciemen, assenyala que estan fent “un procés d’actualització i una crida a un col·lectiu intel·lectual i d’entitats i associacions i del món acadèmic internacional perquè facin aquelles aportacions que permetin tenir una visió actualitzada del document”. D’aquesta manera, volen que el text es converteixi en “un punt de referència a l’hora de legislar ampliacions de constitucions “. De fet, el projecte aspira que les Nacions Unides adoptin formalment aquesta declaració. articles.body: (ACN) Inspecció de Treball ha constatat que l’Institut Municipal de Parcs i Jardins de Barcelona no compleix els requisits mínims de seguretat laboral perquè una part dels vehicles que utilitza la plantilla no disposen de sistemes de climatització . Així ho recull un informe de l’organisme del 15 de setembre elaborat arran d’una denúncia de la CGT . D’aquesta manera, Inspecció de Treball ha requerit a l’empresa municipal que corregeixi les deficiències detectades en els vehicles sense aire condicionat i garanteixi la protecció dels treballadors durant els episodis de calor. També et pot interessar La CGT denuncia desprotecció dels treballadors municipals davant les onades de calor Sandra García Prat 2 minuts de lectura Dos treballadors amb cops de calor Segons la CGT, 127 vehicles van superar els 40 graus a l’interior durant l’estiu i almenys dos treballadors van patir cops de calor . El sindicat va presentar la denúncia abans que es produïssin aquestes incidències laborals i va demanar que es tramités amb caràcter d’urgència. Tot i això, la resolució d’Inspecció de Treball no va arribar fins al setembre. Aquesta conclou que Parcs i Jardins ha establert unes condicions de treball que no compleixen amb els requisits mínims de seguretat establerts per la normativa d’aplicació. Així mateix, assenyala que els vehicles afectats no disposen de climatització, fet que exposa els treballadors a temperatures elevades a l’interior durant els mesos d’estiu. Tant els representants de l’empresa com els del comitè d’empresa van reconèixer aquesta situació durant les compareixences que consten en el document. També et pot interessar Barcelona reparteix polseres per prevenir cops de calor entre els treballadors de Parcs i Jardins Redacció 2 minuts de lectura El 58 % té aire condicionat, diu l’Ajuntament L’Ajuntament assegura que el 58 % de la flota té aire condicionat gràcies que Parcs i Jardins ha impulsat una inversió per instal·lar sistemes de climatització als vehicles. El consistori assegura que s’estan estudiant projectes d’inversió i mesures per estendre l’aire condicionat a més vehicles. Pel que fa als vehicles que aquest estiu encara no disposaven de sistemes de climatització, l’Ajuntament afirma que es va seguir un protocol de prevenció de riscos adaptat a les temperatures. També et pot interessar La CGT denuncia que dos treballadors de Parcs i Jardins han patit cops de calor mentre treballaven Arnau Vaqué 1 minut de lectura Mesures condicionades pel pressupost Durant la investigació , els responsables de Parcs i Jardins van explicar que preveuen instal·lar sistemes de climatització en alguns vehicles i substituir progressivament els que no es poden adaptar. Segons l’informe, però, aquestes actuacions estan condicionades per limitacions pressupostàries que poden dependre també de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona. articles.body: Triar el nom d’un fill no sempre és fàcil. Cal trobar-ne un que convenci i, en cas que hi hagi dos progenitors , posar-se d’acord. Una tasca que es pot convertir en una missió impossible. A banda, com en tot, també hi ha modes . Júlia, Martina, Emma i Sofia van ser els noms femenins més posats l’any 2025 a Catalunya. Els masculins : Biel, Nil, Marc i Jan. Però hi ha noms que sonen antics, que eren populars fa gairebé un segle i que s’estan tornant a posar. Passa als Estats Units , on un estudi va assenyalar el retorn de noms com Eleanor, Violet, Nora i Hazel. Una tornada progressiva durant el segle XXI després de dècades pràcticament desapareguts . El professor de la UB, Jordi Muñoz , va voler comprovar si això també passa amb els noms catalans . Amèlia ha multiplicat per 15 la popularitat Noms com Victòria, Amèlia, Aurora i Emília s’havien convertit en residuals a finals del segle passat . En canvi, en les últimes dècades han multiplicat la seva popularitat. Alguns de manera sorprenent, com Amèlia, que es posa 15 vegades més que en el seu punt més baix. Comencen a tornar també els noms de besàvies catalanes? https://t.co/ix8m3WhrIb pic.twitter.com/bVmqqe8xuL — Jordi Muñoz (@jordimunozm) October 14, 2026 Tot i això, es tracta de noms que segueixen lluny dels més posats. Almenys, per ara. Victòria és un nom que porten tres de cada mil nenes que han nascut en aquesta dècada. Júlia , el més popular, s’ha posat, en el mateix període de temps, a més de 15 de cada mil nenes. També et pot interessar El nom de Mercè, copatrona de Barcelona, ja no es posa a les nenes Clara Vera Colina Marina Sancho 2 minuts de lectura També hi ha noms masculins que remunten el vol En el cas dels noms d’home, també hi ha exemples que segueixen el mateix patró. Mateu ha multiplicat per 13 la seva popularitat. D’altres, com Tomàs, Elies i Fèlix , van tenir el seu punt més baix als anys 80 i 90 del segle passat, però encadenen dècades de crescuda. Tal com passa en els noms femenins, també queden lluny dels més posats. Tomàs és el nom de dos de cada mil nens catalans nascuts a partir del 2020 . En canvi, hi ha més de 13 de cada mil nens nascuts en aquesta dècada que es diuen Nil, el nom més posat . També et pot interessar Quins són els cognoms més comuns a Barcelona el 2026? Consulta-ho en aquesta llista Eva Vial 1 minut de lectura Quins són els noms que han desaparegut? L’investigador de l’ Institut de Biologia Evolutiva de la UPF , Francesc Calafell , ha explicat al programa bàsics que la tendència és que els noms més posats siguin cada vegada més curts. Per contra, indica que “s’han perdut els compostos”. Noms com Josep Maria o Maria del Carme , que havien estat dels més triats, estan prop de desaparèixer . L’efecte dels noms dels famosos Calafell ha apuntat, també, que quan un personatge guanya molta popularitat , pot produir un efecte directe en la freqüència d’us del seu nom. L’efecte pot ser en positiu, com va passar amb Leo durant els anys que Messi jugava al Barça , però també pot ser en negatiu. És el cas, per exemple, de la relació directe entre l’aparició d’ Aïda Nízar , exconcursant de Gran Hermano percebuda com a antipàtica , i la reducció en l’ús d’aquest nom durant els anys posteriors al concurs . articles.body: El Festival Feroe s’ha vist obligat a cancel·lar la seva segona edició , després d’estrenar-se el novembre de l’any 2025 al Poble Espanyol , on van actuar grups com Squeeze o The Tallest Man on Earth. L’organització ha explicat en un comunicat que no s’han venut les entrades necessàries per fer-lo viable . El director del Feroe, Albert Puig, ha especificat que “no hem aconseguit captivar les 2.000 persones necessàries” per tirar endavant aquesta segona edició del festival. Es retornaran els els diners de les entrades comprades fins al moment. També et pot interessar Albert Puig, promotor de Feroe Festival Radio Ext 1 minut de lectura Alternativa a la música de masses A través del comunicat, el periodista musical i promotor Albert Puig, ha lamentat que no continuï el projecte, que volia ser “una alternativa a la música de masses […] on es poguessin veure aquells artistes que, malgrat el seu enorme talent, estan desapareixent de tots els cartells”. A més de la manca de públic, la direcció ha atribuït la cancel·lació també als preus excessius de contractació dels artistes “molts són senzillament indecents”. El director, però, no tanca les portes a començar algun altre projecte de música. “La meva voluntat de perseguir nous models de música en directe més amables i justos segueix intacta”, diu per tancar el comunicat.
articles.headline: Cancel·lada la segona edició del Festival Feroe

articles.body: Els avisos ES-Alert s’han convertit gairebé en habituals les darreres setmanes per la pluja torrencial. Són alertes que suposen un trasbals per a tota la població, però especialment per a les persones que viuen al carrer. Ara, diverses entitats socials, agrupades en la Comissió de Sensellarisme del Grup de Reducció de Danys de Catalunya , han impulsat un manifest perquè les administracions garanteixin un “refugi segur” a les persones sense llar. També et pot interessar Els aiguats i les onades de calor disparen els serveis dels Bombers de Barcelona Arnau Vaqué 2 minuts de lectura Al text, lamenten que “davant les pluges intenses, se’ns està demanant evitar els desplaçaments i quedar-nos en un lloc segur. Mentrestant, les persones que viuen al carrer, en vehicles, horts o barraques continuen exposades a inundacions i riuades que amenacen les seves vides”. Asseguren que “viure al carrer sense alternatives no és una elecció lliure aquests darrers dies estem veient com la protecció davant d’una emergència depèn de tenir un habitatge”. També et pot interessar Gairebé 200 sensellar van pernoctar en allotjaments d’emergència pels aiguats d’octubre a Barcelona Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura 24.000 persones sense llar a Catalunya Afirmen que a Catalunya estan en aquesta situació prop de 24.000 persones i lamenten que “la resposta institucional està sent desigual davant les emergències”. Per això, demanen “garantir allotjaments accessibles, segurs i de proximitat, amb cobertura de totes les formes de sensellarisme, també en assentaments i zones aïllades” i que, a més, s’eliminin “les barreres relacionades amb la documentació, els animals de companyia o la necessitat de conservar les pertinences.” També creuen que caldria incorporar els equips de proximitat, sensellarisme i reducció de danys als dispositius de coordinació de Protecció Civil.
